minutes_text:
Arts Commission

  Inglewood, California
  September 18, 2024

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission was convened on September 18, 2024.
Commissioner Lesure called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Ashley Ferrettte announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Commissioner Aletha Metcalf ‐ District 1, Commissioner Olivia Alvitre –
  District 2, Commissioner Phyllis Battle ‐ District 3, Commissioner Vicki Perryman-
  Banks - District 4, Commissioner Jacques Lesure - Commissioner at Large

City Personnel present were as follows:

  Mark Weinberg  City Manager
  Harjinder Singh  Deputy City Manager
  Ashley Ferrette  Staff Assistant

SPECIAL SPEAKERS
City Manager Mark Weinberg introduced himself to the Arts Commission and initiated a
dialogue about potential ideas for enhancing the program.

    Funding Enhancements:
  o Proposed increasing funding to the program and suggested modifications
  to the Percent for the Arts program:
   Requiring 25% of the 1% (0.25%) contribution to be paid directly
  into the Arts Program Fund.
   Expanding the program to include large residential construction
  projects, requiring a 0.25% contribution to the Arts Program Fund.
  There would be no requirement for onsite art due to public
  accessibility issues associated with residential developments.

    Additional Initiatives:
  o Suggested restarting a grant program for struggling artists outside the
  Public Arts Program.
  o Proposed expanding the use of Public Arts Funds to support programs in
  theater, poetry, and dance.

  1
   Arts Commission

  Mr. Weinberg also discussed transferring the Percent for the Arts Program to the
  Library Services Department. He explained that this change would help balance
  departmental responsibilities and align the program with other cities where
  Percent for the Arts programs are typically managed under library services, which
  often focus on cultural arts and education.

  No actions were taken by the Arts Commission but a request was made to
  continue this dialog.

Deputy City Manager Harjinder Singh provided a comprehensive presentation on the
Inglewood Library and Technology Center Renovation Project.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. Luis Canche, longtime resident and city employee likes the idea of
all the new updates and technology being incorporated into the new Inglewood Library
however; he also thinks it would be a great idea to incorporate some of the city’s historic
culture and art.

MINUTES. None

VERBAL REPORTS-Public Art‐Related Projects.
  a. Inglewood Open Studios Art Walk will be held on November 9 and 10, 2024.

PUBLIC REMARKS. Jorge Gomez, Board Member of the Inglewood Open Studios is
collaborating with Joyce Stallone for this year’s Art Walk. On October 10th, he and his
team will host an artist mixer at the Studio located at 1019 Manchester Boulevard from
5:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. for artists to meet other artists. This event is open to the public.

COMMISSIONERS’ COMMENTS/INITIATIVES/ART CALENDAR.
  a. Next Arts Commission Meeting: October 16, 2024 at 6:30 p.m.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Lesure declared the
meeting adjourned, at 8:03 p.m.
